# S06 — Practices into tools

Research cut: **2026-10-28**. Scope: all 11 specified E ledgers and all five specified Connect ledgers. **Q** = supplied quotation or attributed report; **F** = externally sourced fact; **I** = interpretation/proposal; **E** = estimate. A demonstrated internal tool is evidence of implementation, not of a public package, reliable general performance, demand, or willingness to pay.

**I — Result:** The most repeated practices are proving actual behavior, converting corrections into reusable checks, and simplifying instructions as models change. All three already have public implementations. The strongest remaining opportunities are narrower: **skill invocation/composition fixtures; environment-mismatch diagnostic recipes; and temporal interaction assertions**. These fit an upstream contribution or weekend tool better than another agent platform. Repeated manual work is a discovery signal; it does not establish that existing tools are inadequate.

## Coverage, reading method, and counting

**F — Local evidence:** Read the per-video digests, recurring themes, prior-art triage and top-five sections across E01–E11 and Connect 01–05. Extracted every row whose type contains Practice or Hand-rolled, including lowercase/mixed types, Connect's Hand-built, and Connect 04's H/lesson notation. There are **2,182 retained rows**. Appendix A preserves all of them with ledger location, source-caption location, quotation, interpretation, and packaging disposition. Rows are observations, not 2,182 distinct techniques or opportunities. Historical compiler, database, infrastructure, creator and language-learning techniques remain in the inventory; they were not discarded for being small or outside coding-agent fashion.

**F — Corpus-count discrepancy:** The brief describes 98 recordings (85 corpus + 13 Connect). The specified E01–E11 inventory resolves to **83 distinct numbered corpus caption files plus 13 Connect files, 96 total** in this workspace. All retained practice/forward rows resolve; no source file is invented for the two-count difference. Later `p3-*` transcripts and E12+ ledgers appeared in the shared workspace during research and are outside the explicitly assigned E01–E11/Connect scope. This report does not claim coverage of those additions.

**F/I — Transcript method:** Resolve every retained row to its supplied transcript and timestamp buckets; consult the corresponding caption text for technique details. The central practitioner cases receive closer treatment below. Caption timestamps identify minute buckets, not exact utterance offsets. The row appendix provides the audit trail rather than reproducing entire transcripts. Appendix B also retains all ledger rows explicitly typed Prediction/Roadmap/Pr, including adjacent technical predictions, so the theme-specific board does not silently erase contrary or awkward forecasts.

**F — Background used:** [kill list and research rules](/Users/noah/code/sofort/arch/research/RESEARCH-SUMMARY.md), [stack synthesis](/Users/noah/code/sofort/arch/research/stack/SUMMARY.md), [Connect synthesis](/Users/noah/code/sofort/arch/research/connect26/SUMMARY.md). Generic hosting/durability, orchestration loops, agent JIT/skill compilation, Code Mode, classifiers, broad review/test generation, type-check acceleration, installation platforms, migrations/proofs, and agent-scale Git remain occupied/killed categories. No new evidence here revives those broad pitches. A fixture for an existing mechanism is a different, much smaller deliverable.

**I/E — Independence:** The convergence counts below are conservative, named lower bounds of distinct reporting practitioners, with publishing channels counted separately. The same person across several recordings counts once. Amp's many videos count as one implementation team; Thorsten Ball and Quinn Slack are distinct speakers but are not two independent implementations. Theo on t3.gg and Nerd Snipe counts once. Matt explicitly credits Thariq for the interview idea: two adopters, one acknowledged lineage. Eric Tech's Pstack account is secondary reporting, not Lauren Tan's direct testimony. Ben Davis and Ben Vinegar are different people. Michael Shimeles/Ras Mic describes the four-step workflow on Peter Yang's channel; Peter is not credited as its author. Provider speakers and their customers are not automatically independent confirmations of the same implementation. A source used in two clusters does not become two customers. Counts record people performing or assembling a practice, including their own scripts/skills; they are not counts of unaided repetitions, independent inventions, current unsolved needs, or buyers.

**I — Public-availability vocabulary:** **Shipped** means inspectable public implementation/documentation, or explicitly qualified *internal implementation reported by a speaker*. **Being built** means active work reported by a named owner. **Roadmap** means intent, not availability. **Open** means a bounded residual was not established in inspected prior art; it is not a claim that nobody has built it. Exact row-level distribution is marked unverified where family-level research cannot establish it. No repositories were installed or executed during this research.

Targeted X discovery did not yield inspectable posts that improved primary-source verification; X absence is not evidence of an open gap. No project here depends on an unverified X assertion.

## Project cards

All concepts below are **I**. Source quotations are **Q**. Development time and scores are **E**. Scores are ordered **C / T / G / V / S / N**: cool; Cloudflare/Vercel/TypeScript adjacency; real gap; value; survives better models; distinct from GrowOS. Each is 1–5. High N does not mean a large market. “Owner reason” is a contribution strategy, not a claim the platform owner cannot implement it. Exact residual demand remains unproven. P01–P25 are the complete proposed-project set; appendix packaging hints are evidence dispositions, not thousands of additional endorsed projects.

### P01 — Concrete proof recipes, not a new proof runner

**Tiny; Shipped mechanism / Open content. Manual family N=10, 9 channels.**

- **One sentence:** Contribute a small pack of runnable, baseline-failing examples showing which evidence actually establishes each change type.

- **Closest:** [rstack](https://github.com/michaelshimeles/rstack), [gbrain](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/TESTING.md), [Pstack](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack). Reuse their runners/receipts.

**I — GrowOS test:** There is no well-supported broad “nobody is building it” seed here. The missing parts most supported by independent evidence are mundane integration boundaries: what got loaded, what actually ran, what machine it ran on, what changed over time, and whether the next person can use the output. They can survive better models because those facts are external to model capability. They also have obvious existing owners, so small upstream work is the default route.

## Ranked project table

**I/E — Ranking rule:** Sort by independent practitioners reporting the **underlying manual practice**, then distinguish how many report the narrower proposed failure. This makes prevalence visible without presenting a heavily occupied category as an open market. Counts are the conservative rosters above. A zero in the narrower column means an inferred project, not absent evidence for the parent practice. Ties within a count have no statistical meaning. The recommended build bets below additionally consider current prior art and whether a small contribution can demonstrate something useful.

Scores are **C/T/G/V/S/N**, each 1–5; they are judgments, not measured outcomes. “Open” always means the exact bounded residual is provisional.

### Top three build bets after removing shipped broad ideas

1. **P03 — Skill invocation/composition conformance corpus.** The strongest bounded contribution: turn real, already-fixed Pstack/Matt defects into regression fixtures over actual invocation, metadata, paths and harness entry points. Reuse skill-up/Pstack; ask maintainers to accept the fixtures. A weekend prototype can establish whether the residual exists.
2. **P05 — Environment-mismatch recipe pack.** Four independent concrete variants across four channels. Start with stale executable identity and immutable Git configuration, then target OS and region-specific provider parameters. Contribute to an existing diagnostic/history tool if its extension surface fits.
3. **P15 — Temporal interaction assertions.** Package the ad hoc frame-by-frame and rapid-interaction checks as a few explicit TS assertions with traces and violating frames. Check existing visual-tool APIs before building; recording by itself is already solved.

These are build recommendations, not the top three prevalence counts. The most prevalent families already have useful packages. All three recommendations have a quick stop condition and can end as a small upstream PR rather than a standalone product.

### Most surprising signal

**Q:** Ben Davis says the workflow-development conversation is “poison” because it already knows too much, then has a fresh agent impersonate him and replay his original prompts [V31 · 15:00](/Users/noah/code/sofort/arch/research/corpus/transcripts/31-ben-davis-how-i-m-actually-using-ai-these-days.txt:19). Amp independently gives fresh Orbs ordinary, unhinted tasks and checks the actual traces [V39 · 01:00](/Users/noah/code/sofort/arch/research/corpus/transcripts/39-amp-inc-using-orbs-to-eval-agent-friendliness.txt:5). **I:** a successful authoring session is a poor test of whether a reusable workflow is self-contained. The surprising market correction is that even this advanced technique is already packaged: skill-up supports simulated users and Pstack documents blind evaluation. The useful contribution is the realistic fixture and invocation evidence, not another evaluator. Davis's replay includes steering, so it is evidence of assisted improvement, not unassisted reliability.

### Five-line TL;DR

1. **F:** Catalogue: 2,182 practice/hand-built rows, 823 explicit forward-claim rows, with ledger and caption links.
2. **I/E:** Proving behavior, preserving corrections and deleting obsolete scaffolding have the most independent convergence.
3. **F:** tstack, rstack, Matt's skills, Pstack, skill-up and Code Insights already package much of that work.
4. **I:** Best small bets: invocation fixtures, environment-mismatch recipes and temporal interaction assertions.
5. **I:** Keep the one-person niches; build a concrete reusable example, then stop if existing tools already cover it.
